company: Six Flags Entertainment Corporation (post-merger of Cedar Fair + Six Flags)

rfm_tuples.R: 'Management plans to achieve cost synergies through operating cost reductions, organizational restructurings and elimination of duplicative overhead costs, including redundant processes and technologies.' Project Accelerate objective (2): 'identify and activate operating efficiencies that generate cost synergies and drive margin expansion.' Mergers closed July 1, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: Synergy quantification candor. A post-merger thesis stands or falls on the synergy run-rate. Look for whether management quantifies the $-amount of cost synergies anywhere in the 10-K, or whether the disclosure relies entirely on qualitative language ('drive margin expansion', 'achieving cost synergies'). Compare to the Cedar Fair investor-day public commitments around the merger announcement (Nov 2023).
rfm_tuples.M_source: filing_internal_absence (no synergy quantification anywhere in 10-K text)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Across the entire 408KB 10-K text, ZERO dollar quantification of expected synergies appears. 'Synergy/synergies' appears 11 times — every instance is either (a) risk-factor disclaimer language ('may not be realized fully or at all'), (b) Project Accelerate narrative, or (c) goodwill rationale ('primarily attributable to expected synergies'). NO $/timing commitment ($X by 20YY) is given. The merger was announced Nov 2, 2023 with Cedar Fair/Six Flags publicly targeting ~$200M run-rate synergies; the 10-K filed 8 months post-close avoids restating any target.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A merger-of-equals 10-K that refuses to quantify the synergy run-rate eight months after close, when goodwill of $3.08B was booked PRIMARILY on the basis of those synergies, is a textbook Mode-B disclosure-evasion signal. Either (a) the synergy capture is behind plan and management is not yet ready to commit to a number, or (b) the realized 2024 synergies were de minimis. Either way, the $3.08B goodwill cushion rests on a number the company will not name in the 10-K.

rfm_tuples.R: 'For the year ended December 31, 2024, net revenues increased $910.3 million compared with 2023. The increase ... reflected the impact of a 15.0 million-visit increase in attendance and a $40.2 million increase in out-of-park revenues, partially offset by the impact of a $0.90, or 1.4% decrease in in-park per capita spending. The 15.0 million-visit increase in attendance included a 14.2 million-visit increase resulting from attendance at Former Six Flags parks during the six months ended December 31, 2024.' Attendance 41,649K (FY24) vs 26,665K (FY23) — +56.2%. In-park per capita $61.31 vs $62.21 — (1.4)%.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A + B: Attendance/per-capita honesty. Mode-A: are the figures stated unambiguously? Yes. Mode-B (more important): on a like-for-like basis, what was attendance trend? 14.2M of the 15.0M attendance increase = Former Six Flags acquired parks. Cedar Fair organic attendance change is therefore only +0.8M visits on a base of ~26.7M = +3%. PRO FORMA twelve-month attendance comparison is NOT disclosed (only revenue/loss). What did pro-forma combined-co attendance do in 2024 vs 2023?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pro forma net revenues: $3,284,971K (2024) vs $3,232,378K (2023) — only +1.6% on a combined-company basis. Pro forma net loss: $(344,416)K vs $(76,579)K — loss widened by $267.8M YoY. CRITICALLY: the company discloses pro-forma revenue and net loss but NOT pro-forma attendance or pro-forma in-park per capita. The 1.4% per-capita decline IS disclosed (good), but the $0.90 absolute decline was 'due to a planned decrease in average season pass pricing' — confirming admission price erosion at Former Cedar Fair.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The headline 56.2% attendance growth is purely acquisition arithmetic — Former Six Flags parks added for 6 months. On a like-for-like basis, pro-forma revenue grew only 1.6% while pro-forma net loss expanded 4.5x. Management discloses pro-forma revenue/loss (technically required by ASC 805) but conspicuously omits pro-forma attendance and pro-forma per-capita — the two operating KPIs the company itself flags as 'the primary drivers of financial and operational performance.' This is selective pro-forma disclosure: the metrics that work get stated GAAP-headline style; the metrics that don't get omitted from the combined narrative. Classic Mode-B catch.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the third quarter of 2024, management tested the Schlitterbahn reporting unit's fair value due to a decline in estimated future cash flows as a result of shifting investment priorities at those locations following the Mergers. Management concluded the estimated fair value of the Schlitterbahn reporting unit no longer exceeded its carrying value. Therefore, a $42.5 million impairment of the goodwill related to the Schlitterbahn reporting unit was recorded during the third quarter of 2024.' Plus: 'These reporting units' [list of 9 Six Flags parks including Magic Mountain, Great Adventure, Great America, Mexico, Over Georgia, Over Texas, New England, Fiesta Texas] fair value exceeded their carrying values by less than 10% upon allocation. If future operating results do not meet expectations, the goodwill assigned to these reporting units may become impaired.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: derive forward impairment probability. A <10% cushion on NINE separate Six Flags reporting units, combined with a confirmed FY24 impairment at Schlitterbahn (a Cedar Fair-era acquisition) just months after a $3.08B Mergers goodwill addition, implies very high probability of additional impairment in FY25 if operations don't accelerate. Test consistency with auditor critical-audit-matter and pro-forma loss trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total goodwill $3,296.5M (FY24) vs $264.6M (FY23) — almost all is post-merger allocation. Nine Six Flags reporting units have <10% cushion. Pro-forma net loss widened from -$76.6M to -$344.4M YoY (4.5x). Deloitte's SOLE critical audit matter is Schlitterbahn goodwill — the SMALLEST reporting unit, signaling auditor focus on subjective-cash-flow assumptions even where the dollars are modest. Operating income $310.5M but net loss $206.7M because interest expense ballooned to $234.8M and tax provision was $240.8M (tax on partnership conversion).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Nine reporting units with <10% cushion plus an already-impaired Schlitterbahn unit plus widening pro-forma losses plus shrinking organic attendance growth = a goodwill-impairment-loaded balance sheet. If any of the Six Flags legacy parks misses 2025 plan (which is likely given combined-co pro-forma losses are widening, not narrowing), the impairment could be hundreds of millions. The 'less than 10%' disclosure is HONEST (this is good) — but the implication that management/auditor are aware impairment is one bad-quarter-away is what Mode B should escalate.

rfm_tuples.R: 'With the Combined Company's revolving credit facility and cash on hand, the Combined Company has sufficient liquidity to satisfy existing cash obligations at least through the first quarter of 2026.' Debt schedule: $200M 7.000% senior secured notes maturing July 2025 (classified as current maturities of $210M); $500M 5.375% senior unsecured notes April 2027; $500M 5.500% senior unsecured notes April 2027; $300M 6.500% senior unsecured notes Oct 2028; $500M 5.250% senior unsecured notes July 2029; $995M term loan May 2031; $800M 7.250% senior unsecured notes May 2031; $850M 6.625% senior secured notes May 2032. Plus $315M outstanding on $850M revolver (springing maturity July 2029). Total notes $4,960M + revolver $315M + term loan $995M = ~$6.27B gross debt. Cash $83.2M.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: liquidity-horizon framing. Standard 10-K liquidity language commits to '12 months from filing date' (i.e., March 2026). FUN commits only 'through the first quarter of 2026' — Q1 2026 ends ~March 31 2026, which is BARELY 12 months from the March 3, 2025 filing date. Test whether this is an unusually narrow horizon and whether the $200M July 2025 maturity is covered.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cash $83.2M + $315M drawn revolver = available revolver ~$535M (less letters of credit). $200M July 2025 maturity is covered (already in current portion, will be paid from revolver/term refi). HOWEVER: $1.0B of 2027 maturities (April 2027 — both Six Flags 2027 Six Notes 5.50% AND Cedar Fair 2027 Notes 5.375%) sit 24 months after cutoff. Interest expense $234.8M in 2024 (only 6 months of Six Flags debt). Full-year run-rate interest will be ~$330-350M on $6.3B at blended ~5.7%. Operating income $310.5M; full-year run-rate post-merger interest exceeds operating income.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'sufficient through Q1 2026' language is the MINIMUM that allows avoiding going-concern flag — exactly 12 months. Compared to the typical 'foreseeable future' language, this is a narrow horizon. The structural issue: $1.0B refinancing wall in April 2027 against a combined-company that just lost $344M pro-forma and where full-year interest expense will exceed operating income. The dividend was cut to zero ('has not declared a dividend and has no immediate plans to do so') — Cedar Fair's storied distribution history is over. The 'no immediate plans' for dividends is the practical admission that capital must be redirected to debt service.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In December 2024, the Combined Company elected to purchase all of the outstanding limited partnership interests in Six Flags Over Georgia and White Water Atlanta in 2027. The Combined Company will be required to make an election regarding Six Flags Over Texas by December 31, 2025.' 'NCI call option liability' $290.4M on balance sheet (FY24). 'Redeemable non-controlling interests' $241.8M. Implied valuation of Partnership Parks using Specified Price if determined as of Dec 31, 2024 = $409.7M.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: derive the off-balance-sheet/contingent liability magnitude. Partnership Parks obligations are pre-merger Six Flags liabilities the Combined Company assumed. The Dec 2024 election to BUY Georgia/White Water in 2027 commits cash; Texas election due Dec 2025. In event of default, 'Time Warner has the right to take control of the Partnership Parks. rfm_tuples.M_value: Partnership Parks total commitment $409.7M (Specified Price). $290.4M NCI Call Option already on balance sheet. Texas election due Dec 31, 2025 — well within FY25, will require similar accrual. Cross-default to 2024 Credit Agreement if Combined Company defaults on Partnership Parks obligations. Time Warner retains takeover rights. These are 1998-vintage liabilities Cedar Fair inherited via the merger.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Combined Company is essentially forced to pay ~$400M+ for the Partnership Park interests in 2027-2028 — the SAME window as the $1.0B April 2027 senior notes maturity wall. The Time-Warner-cross-default mechanism means failure to meet partnership cash calls triggers credit-agreement default. This is a hidden liability that adds to the 2027 refinancing pressure. Management's '12-month liquidity sufficient' framing does not address this 24-36-month cliff.

rfm_tuples.R: Modified EBITDA $899.8M (FY24) vs $527.7M (FY23). Adjustments to reconcile included: $118.3M 'Costs related to the Mergers' (third-party legal/consulting, integration costs, retention bonuses, severance, contract terminations, maintenance to update Former Six Flags parks to Cedar Fair standards, onboarding new advertising firms, travel). $14.9M 'Self-insurance adjustment.' $30.6M 'Non-cash foreign currency loss.' $63.8M 'Non-cash equity compensation.' Modified EBITDA margin 33.2% vs 29.3%.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: assess add-back aggressiveness. $118.3M of merger/integration costs being added back to EBITDA is large but generally accepted; however, the inclusion of 'maintenance costs to update Former Six Flags parks to Cedar Fair standards' as a one-time add-back is more aggressive — these are operational standard-setting expenses that will recur as the integration continues. Also: the prior-year Modified EBITDA margin (29.3%) is being compared to a 33.2% margin that benefits from these $148M+ of add-backs.
rfm_tuples.M_value: $118.3M merger costs add-back includes: 'maintenance costs to update Former Six Flags parks to Cedar Fair standards' — operational maintenance disguised as one-time integration. $14.9M self-insurance 'adjustment' (one-time?). $30.6M FX (genuinely non-cash). $63.8M equity comp (recurring cash equivalent). Excluding equity comp + maintenance-disguised-as-integration, true cash-EBITDA materially lower. Pro-forma 12-month net loss $344M; pro-forma net loss margin -10.5%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Modified EBITDA construct allows management to display 33.2% margin while the underlying combined business is losing $344M pro-forma. The most aggressive add-back is treating standards-alignment maintenance as a one-time integration cost (it will recur as more Six Flags parks are 'updated'). Equity comp $63.8M is also added back though it is a real economic cost. The Adjusted-EBITDA-improvement narrative is a covenant-compliance construct, not an honest measure of combined-company economics.

summary: FUN exhibits a structurally weak post-merger profile but a CLEAN insider/auditor governance signature — these point in opposite directions under the honesty-alpha framework. The 10-K's disclosure-evasion signals are economic (no synergy $-quantification despite $3.08B of merger goodwill rationalized 'primarily' by synergies; selective pro-forma disclosure that includes revenue/loss but omits attendance/per-capita) rather than forensic. Five reinforcing weaknesses: (1) refusal to quantify the synergy run-rate that justifies $3.08B of new goodwill; (2) headline 56.2% attendance growth is entirely Six Flags acquisition arithmetic — pro-forma combined-co revenue grew only 1.6% while pro-forma net loss widened 4.5x to $344M; (3) NINE Six Flags reporting units have <10% goodwill cushion plus Schlitterbahn already took $42.5M impairment — high probability of further FY25 writedowns; (4) $1.0B April 2027 refinancing wall plus $400M Partnership Parks 2027-2028 cash obligation against full-year run-rate interest ($330-350M) exceeding operating income (~$310M), with liquidity language committing only to the minimum 12-month Q1 2026 horizon and dividend eliminated; (5) Modified EBITDA construct includes recurring maintenance disguised as one-time integration. OFFSETTING SIGNALS (these weaken the short thesis): CFO Witherow continuity, Deloitte 21-year stability, no Q4 2024 10b5-1 anomalies, no auditor disagreements, Former Six Flags pension actually in surplus ($9.6M), and impairment cushion <10% IS honestly disclosed. Net assessment: this is a structurally-impaired post-merger franchise being managed by a non-deceiving team — exactly the JACK pattern WITHOUT the forensic red flags. Under honesty-alpha framework, the disclosures are largely candid (with notable economic-framing evasion on synergies and pro-forma KPIs), so the composite reflects mostly-disclosed weakness with selective optimism — moderate signal, not strong.
